questions.text: Two AAA cells alone cannot run a Wi-Fi chip: common Wi-Fi chips need at least 3.0 V, and two AAA cells give that only when brand new. How should the device get its power?
options: (recommended) Add a tiny voltage converter after the cells: still only two AAA cells, about +1.5 USD and no visible size change, uses about 85 % of the battery
Use a premium low-voltage Wi-Fi module that runs straight from the cells: allows near-instant remote commands (see q2) but about +12 USD per unit, total about 35 USD, above the 25 USD target
Keep the cells strictly direct with a standard Wi-Fi chip: batteries last weeks, not a year
questions.why: Conflict C1 (must-level): ESP32-class Wi-Fi needs 3.0-3.6 V; a fresh alkaline pair is 3.2 V and falls to 2.0 V; relay coils also need about 2.4 V.

questions.text: The schedule and room temperature control always run on the device without Wi-Fi. How quickly must a change made from the phone or server (for example 'heat room 1 now') reach the device, given one year on a pair of AAA cells?
options: (recommended) Within 30 minutes: about 1.3 years per pair of cells if the firmware connects fast, about 8 months otherwise
Within 60 minutes: more than 1 year even with ordinary firmware
Within seconds: only with the premium Wi-Fi module of q1 (+12 USD), about 1.2 years
Within 5 minutes with the standard chip: batteries last about 2-3.5 months
questions.why: Conflict C2: 1 year allows at most 80 uA average; each Wi-Fi check-in costs about 26-60 uAh.

questions.text: How does the user change the batteries?
options: (recommended) Pull off the cover plate; the cells face the user and all 230 V parts are hidden behind the board, so no electrician is needed. The device is at most 30 mm deep
An electrician removes the device from the box to change cells: allows a slightly smaller board but mains wires are exposed during the change
Cells reachable from the front through a hatch in a custom cover plate: easiest for the user, but needs a custom plate (cost and tooling, larger front)
questions.why: Conflicts C3/C4: the cells, two relays and the 6 mm safety gap only fit in the 503 box with parts on both faces of the board; battery access decides which face points outward and is a safety requirement (no live parts reachable).

questions.text: What must the 25 USD per unit include?
options: (recommended) Board with relays, battery holder and the two temperature probes with 2 m cable; the cover plate and frame come from the wall-plate series already installed. Estimate 21-26 USD, mid about 23
Everything, including a blank 3-module cover plate and frame: estimate 24-32 USD, so cheaper parts or about 28-30 USD
The bare board only, probes bought separately: estimate 18-23 USD, comfortable margin
questions.why: Conflict C5: rough BOM at JLCPCB/LCSC prices for 10 units.
